title: Product sync — rev B drift

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, let's get started.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Short one today. Three things: the Solenne drift ticket, sleep mode, and where rev C is.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Want me to take the drift first?

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Yeah, go.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: So Solenne sent a ticket in on Monday. Two units, humidity channel.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Reading about four percent high after a week in the field.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Four percent of reading, or four points of RH?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Points. They caught it against their reference probe.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That's not nothing for a cold-chain customer.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: No. They're logging vaccine storage. They noticed it right away.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Is it the sensor?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Don't know yet. My guess is the thermistor reference curve.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: The humidity compensation leans on it. If the curve's stale, you drift with temperature.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: That would explain why it grows over the week. Temperature cycling.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Right. That's the theory. I need to reproduce it on a rev B unit first.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Can you do that this week?

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yeah. I've got a bench unit, and the chamber's free Wednesday.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good. And I'll ask Solenne for the two serial numbers.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Please. I want to know if they're from the same lot.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: I'll do it today.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay. Tomas, sleep mode.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: So I started the rewrite on Friday. Not a lot to show yet.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Right now it's sitting around three hundred microamps, which is why the field units are dying in nine days.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Nine days. We promised thirty.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Yeah. Spec is thirty. We're at nine.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Where's the current actually going?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Mostly the radio wake timer. And the sensor rail never powers down between samples.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: The rewrite gates the rail. And stretches the wake interval.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Does that touch calibration timing?

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Shouldn't. Sample cadence stays the same. I'll double check.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Can you put a meter on a rev B unit first? So we have a real baseline.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Yeah. Tomorrow. Real number, not the datasheet guess.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Great. Inès, rev C.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: So rev C is at the fab. Boards went in last Thursday.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: I'd say three weeks.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Three weeks until we have boards in hand?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Boards back, yeah. Then a few days of incoming inspection.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Does rev C change the thermistor?

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: New part, tighter tolerance. So it should help with drift in hardware.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Can't count on that, though. Rev B is what's in the field.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Agreed. Those units need the firmware fix.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Right. So the patch is the real answer for anyone already shipped.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yep.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Okay, let me read back what I've got.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Maya reproduces the drift on a rev B unit. Tomas measures sleep current on rev B. I ask Solenne for the serials.

segments.speaker: spk_1
segments.text: Sounds right.

segments.speaker: spk_0
segments.text: Yeah, that's it.

segments.speaker: spk_2
segments.text: Nothing from me until the boards land.

segments.speaker: local
segments.text: Good. Thanks everyone, that's us.

summary_markdown:
## Key decisions

- The Solenne humidity-channel drift is treated as a firmware problem first: reproduce it on a rev B unit before blaming the sensor.
- Sleep-mode current gets a proper baseline measurement on rev B before the rewrite goes any further.
- Rev C is expected back from the fab in about three weeks, but rev B units already in the field will need the firmware fix regardless.

## Discussion

Maya reported a ticket from Solenne Biolabs: two units showing the humidity channel reading roughly four points high after a week in the field. Solenne logs vaccine storage and caught it against their own reference probe. Maya suspects the thermistor reference curve used by the humidity compensation is stale, which would make the error grow with temperature cycling. Tomas reported that the sleep-mode rewrite has just started; deep-sleep current is around 300µA today, which is why field units last about nine days against a thirty-day spec. The current goes mostly to the radio wake timer and a sensor rail that never powers down between samples. Inès confirmed rev C boards are at the fab, about three weeks out, with a new, tighter-tolerance thermistor that should help at the hardware level but does nothing for rev B in the field.

## Action items

Three items were assigned: Maya reproduces the drift on a rev B unit, Tomas measures sleep-mode current on rev B, and the owner asks Solenne for the serial numbers of the two affected units.

## Open questions

- Whether the two affected Solenne units come from the same lot.
- Whether gating the sensor rail has any effect on calibration timing.
notes_markdown:
- Solenne: 2 units, humidity ~4 pts high after a week. Cold-chain customer, so it matters
- Maya thinks stale thermistor curve, not the sensor. Needs a rev B repro first
- Sleep mode ~300µA today = 9 day battery life vs 30 promised
- Rev C at fab, ~3 weeks. Won't help rev B units already out there
